Spot identification: 4WF-4-WAY-SR-607, flop T8h6c, hero MP holding 9h9d in a 4-way SRP. UTG opened 2.5bb, hero flatted, CO and BTN both flatted, BB folded; hero faces a 25%-pot c-bet from UTG with CO and BTN still to act behind. Hero is OOP-middle with 2 villains behind, the worst seat to defend an underpair.

Per-villain range chains: UTG's open-then-25%-c-bet range on this connected T-high board is wide and value-heavy at the top: TT/88/66 sets, 99 chops (one combo), T9s/T8s/87s two-pair-or-pair-plus-draw, JJ-AA overpairs, KQ/QJ/AQ broadway air with backdoors, plus 79s/97s straight-completing combos. Composition skews value because the board hammers his early-position range. CO flatted UTG preflop range-capped (no AA/KK/AK that would 3-bet); CO's continuance range to a 25% c-bet retains T-x (TT-rare/T9s/AT-occasional), 88-66, 89s/J9s gutshots-plus-overs, and floats. BTN flatted preflop is similarly capped, even wider for suited connectors that hit this board hard (T9s/97s/87s/76s), making BTN's call-or-raise range dense in pair-plus-draw and made-straight combos.

Equity/range tensions: 99 is an underpair to the T, blocking exactly zero of UTG's sets and overpairs, and crushed by every T-x and most two-pairs. Multiway realisation factor for an underpair OOP-middle in a 4-way pot drops to ~0.75 of raw equity. Even raw equity vs UTG's c-bet range is ~22-28%; with two callers still to act, true equity is sub-20% because CO/BTN continuance ranges include the T-x and straight combos hero is dominated by. Pot odds are 2.5/15 = 16.7%, which is the absolute floor and assumes no squeeze.

Spot-specific factors: hero is OOP-middle with squeeze pressure from two players closing action behind; even a call lets CO float wide IP and BTN can raise to charge hero's capped continuance. Set-mining odds require implied odds hero will not realise OOP MW on a flop already dominated by villains' connected hands. 9 is a dead card to draw to and one of only 2 outs left.

Decision: FOLD. Bucket dictates that an underpair below the top board card, OOP-middle with two players to act behind in a 4-way SRP, has no profitable continuance.

Adjacent alternatives: CALL is dominated by squeeze risk + sub-pot-odds realisation; RAISE turns 99 into a pure bluff against a c-bet range that doesn't fold its better-than-99 portion.

BTN's flat range is positional and biased to suited connectors and middle pairs that play well multiway IP — 65s, 87s, 89s, T9s, 76s plus medium pairs and suited broadway floats. Equity/range tensions: hero has top pair good kicker but on a board where every villain's range is loaded with two-pair, sets, straights, and flush draws. Check preserves optionality to check-call CO's c-bet, check-raise vs multiway action with semi-bluffed value, and fold cleanly when 2+ villains take aggressive action behind. Pot-cascade dynamics: a 4-way checked-back flop is unlikely; CO will c-bet often, condensing the field for turn.

Decision: CHECK. Bucket-mandated default for BB closing 4-way SRP on a wet board with TPGK — check-call or check-fold downstream as action dictates.

Adjacent alternatives: BET is dominated by 3-villain squeeze risk and range imbalance; the bet line costs hero more EV by inviting raises from FD+pair-plus-equity than checking and navigating per villain.

Decision: FOLD. Underpair OOP HU facing a flop raise on a high-card single-FD board, with required equity (~46%) exceeding range equity (~34%) and no clean redraw, is a fold.

Adjacent alternatives: CALL is the close alternative; viable if BTN's bluff fraction is higher than range-construction suggests, but on solver-aligned BTN ranges the math favours FOLD. RAISE/jam is dominated — TT has no fold equity vs J-x value and is dominated when called.

SB's overcall range is range-capped and skewed to suited connectors with one-suit and small pairs; on monotone spades SB checks the made-flush (rare) and the FD-with-pair (5s4s/5s9s rare). BB's defence range is the widest and includes more low spades (any Xs broadway, suited connectors with spade); BB's check on monotone is standard.

Equity/range tensions: hero has the nut-flush draw (As is the absolute nut-FD blocker) with 9 spades + 6 outs to TPGK (3 aces + 3 kings, weighted down for board interaction). Raw equity vs the 4-way range is ~45-50% (nut-FD blocker + 2 overs on a board where villains' made-flush fraction is low after MW check). Multiway realisation factor IP-closing with the nut blocker is ~0.85 because hero's blocker collapses villains' best-equity portion. Pot odds N/A (facing_bet=0); SPR is large at 75bb effective.

Spot-specific factors: per `reference_corrections.md` MW-47 corrects to RAISE/aggressive action, anchoring this spot to the aggressive line. Hero IP-closing with nut-FD blocker on monotone MW: (1) bets for value vs weaker FDs (Ks-Xs, Qs-Xs may call), pairs-with-spade, and the rare overpair-with-spade — these all have decent equity vs hero so betting denies their equity-realisation; (2) generates fold equity from no-spade air; (3) realises hero's equity efficiently because villains rarely check-raise without the nut-flush (which hero blocks). Sizing 66% solver-aligned for flop on monotone wet boards — large enough to charge weaker FDs and protect against runner-runner two-pair from no-spade overs, small enough to keep weaker spade equity in.

Decision: BET 66% of pot. Bucket is `nut-FD-blocker-IP-closing-MW` and the action follows from blocker + equity-denial + fold-equity-generation.

Adjacent alternatives: CHECK back is defensible at lower frequencies (realisation insurance), but loses the value+protection EV; BET 25% gives weaker spades a free river card too cheaply on this draw-heavy texture.

Spot identification: 4WF-MW-AXIS-516, flop Jc2s4d, hero BB holding JsTc in a 4-way SRP. CO opens 2.5bb, BTN flats, SB flats, hero defends BB. CO's c-bet range on dry boards in MW is condensed to value + few semibluff candidates (no FDs on rainbow, only gutshots like 35/A3 backdoor). BTN's preflop flat range is capped (no AA/KK/AK) and includes pocket pairs (22-99 set candidates), suited broadway (KJs/QJs etc.), suited connectors that miss J42 (76s/65s/87s air). SB's overcall after CO+BTN is similarly capped and biased to small pairs and suited connectors with multiway equity.

Equity/range tensions: hero TPGK with T kicker is dominated by KJ/QJ/AJ (all in CO's open and possibly BTN's flat) but ahead of weaker J-x (J9s rare), pocket pairs below J, and air floats. Multiway realisation factor BB OOP-early 4-way is ~0.75; against CO's c-bet range hero's raw equity ~45-50% drops to ~38-42% realised. Spot-specific factors: per brief AMENDMENT 1, hero is OOP-early with three villains behind — donk-lead is structurally dominated because it announces a polarised range (no support from hero's BB check range), invites raises from CO's KJ+/sets/overpairs, and forfeits the natural check-raise defence line. Check preserves optionality: (1) check-call CO's c-bet to pot-control TPGK; (2) check-raise vs a small c-bet with discount for protection; (3) check-fold if MW action escalates. Decision: CHECK. Bucket-mandated default for OOP-early BB with TPGK in 4-way SRP on dry boards.

Adjacent alternatives: BET (donk-lead) is dominated by squeeze risk + range imbalance + the structural problem of leading the worst possible range composition; even at small sizing hero pays for an inferior line.

Spot identification: 4WF-MW-AXIS-560, turn 4h4c4dQs, hero SB holding TcTd in a 4-way SRP that checked through 4-way on the flop. Preflop CO opens 2.5bb, BTN flats, hero completes SB, BB defends. Flop 4-4-4 went check-check-check-check (4-way checked through). Turn brings Qs — first overcard since the trips board. Hero is OOP-early first to act on turn; facing_bet=0.

Per-villain range chains: CO's preflop open kept any overpair candidate (AA/KK/QQ/JJ) but the flop check-back of 4-4-4 with overpair-or-QQ is plausible in MW for slowplay (trips with QQ is QQ44 = quads-board-plus-pocket-Q? actually QQ + 4-4-4-Q = full house Q's full of 4's, monster). However QQ usually opens or c-bets the flop trips board for thin value-MW. CO's checked-back range on 4-4-4 flop is wide — includes overpairs that pot-control, broadway air with backdoors, suited Ax. Turn Q gives CO any QQ that slowplayed full-house; AQ/KQ/QJ now top-pair. BTN's preflop flat range capped excludes AA/KK/QQ (would 3-bet a portion); BTN's flop check-behind range is essentially all hands that aren't quads. BB's defence range is widest; turn Q gives BB Q-x value and bluffcatch with pocket pairs (88-JJ).

Equity/range tensions: hero TT + board 4-4-4-Q = full house, fours full of tens. Dominated only by QQ (quads + Q? — no, QQ + 4-4-4-Q = Q's full of 4's, which beats 4's full of 10's) and any pocket pair higher than T (JJ would be J's full of 4's — actually JJ + 4-4-4 = 4-4-4-J-J = 4's full of Js, beats 4's full of T's; same for QQ/KK/AA). So TT is beaten by JJ+ pocket pairs only. Beats all Q-x, all under-pairs, all unpaired hands. In CO/BTN/BB ranges, JJ+ is rare but possible (CO mostly opens JJ+ — would slowplay JJ-AA on 4-4-4? plausible). Effectively hero is ahead of ~85% of villain combined range, behind ~10-15% to higher full houses.

Spot-specific factors: hero is OOP-early on turn with three villains behind. Per brief AMENDMENT 1, donk-leading OOP-early is typically dominated — but on a quads board the donk-lead bucket inverts: hero's range is effectively merged (everyone has trips at minimum; pocket pairs play differently). The standard line on quads turn with under-Q pocket pair is a small lead (33% solver-aligned turn) for thin value from Q-x bluffcatchers and pocket pairs below T (88/99 — wait those also have 4's full so anything under T beats T-T? no: 88+4-4-4-Q = 4-4-4-Q-8 = trips with Q+8 kickers, NOT a full house since 8-8 doesn't make a pair on a board with three 4's and one Q. Hmm wait — full house requires 3-of-a-kind plus a pair. Board 4-4-4-Q has trips. Hero 8-8 + board gives 4-4-4-8-8 = 4's full of 8's. So pocket pairs DO make full houses. So hero TT beats 8-8/9-9 full houses but loses to JJ/QQ/KK/AA full houses. Beats unpaired hands which play the board (4-4-4-Q-Hero's-highest-card).

Decision: BET 33% of pot. Thin value lead for: pocket pairs 22-99 (smaller full houses), Q-x calls (trips + Q kicker), and bluffcatch from broadway floats. Sizing small because villains' fold-everything-worse threshold is low; protection minimal since most folding hands are drawing dead anyway.

Adjacent alternatives: CHECK to induce is defensible at meaningful frequency (let villains bluff or value-bet worse pairs into hero), and is the safer line vs the JJ+ slowplay risk; mixed 50/50 BET-small / CHECK-call is plausible. RAISE n/a (facing_bet=0). The lean to BET is for thin EV from broadway+small-pair calls.
